I've built and pushed Haq in four commits, but none of the Claude-powered parts have actually run yet. There's no `.env`, so I have no `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` or `NEATLOGS_API_KEY`.

**To continue:** create `.env` from `.env.example`, fill in both keys, and tell me when it's done. I won't print or commit them. I'll then do one interview plus a full run on one household, run the evals (first on a couple of households, then all 20), commit the results file and fix whatever breaks.

**What I've tested so far:**
- The server starts, serves the page and creates a household.
- The page fetcher works against real government sites. It recovered from a simulated failure, retried an expired certificate on sspy-up.gov.in, and moved from pmjay.gov.in (timed out) to another official page.
- The eval scoring works on made-up predictions.

**What's built:**
- **App** (`app.py`, `static/index.html`): a big Hindi mic button with a text box fallback. Questions and answers are spoken aloud in Hindi. Results are large cards with an emoji, the ₹ per year, which family member, documents needed, where to apply and an official source link, under a headline total.
  - A family that comes back sees its saved results and can ask follow-up questions.
  - Any search that was interrupted resumes when the server restarts.
- **Agent** (`haq/agent.py`): a short Hindi interview (it never asks about caste), then a plan of candidate schemes per member. Each scheme then gets its own research loop using web search and an official-page fetch tool.
  - The code rejects a scheme unless every eligibility rule cites an official page the agent actually read. Unverifiable schemes are dropped, and disagreements with unofficial sites are logged with a reason.
- **Recovery** (`haq/fetcher.py`): each page is tried 3 times with increasing waits, then the scheme's other official pages are tried. `SIMULATE_FAILURE=1` makes the first lookup fail for the demo.
- **State**: everything is saved to `data/state.json` after every step, so families can return and a crashed run picks up where it stopped.
- **Tracing**: every Claude call, agent step and tool call is traced in neatlogs, grouped by household.
- **Evals**:
  - `evals/families.json` has 20 UP households and 55 expected schemes, each with an official source URL and `needs_human_check: true`. It includes negative cases, such as a farmer who pays income tax being excluded from PM-KISAN and a divorced mother not getting the widow pension.
  - `run_evals.py` reports precision, recall, accuracy, average cost and average time, and saves `evals/results-<timestamp>.json` with the change from the previous run.

**Please check:**
- **Eval answers:** several state portals only load content with JavaScript or had broken pages, so some rules and amounts are from my own knowledge plus the portal home pages. Two to spot-check first:
  - the income limits for the UP pensions
  - whether the UP pension limits rule out the joint family in household h12 (I marked that pension optional)
- **Insecure retry:** when a government site's security certificate has expired, the fetcher retries once without checking it. It only reads public pages and logs that it did this.
- **Insurance schemes don't count either way in scoring:** insurance and contributory products (PMJJBY, PMSBY, PM-SYM, e-Shram, crop insurance) are marked "acceptable extra". Haq isn't penalised for finding or missing them. The README explains this.
- **Fallback setting:** I turned on Anthropic's refusal fallback, which retries a declined request on another model within the same call. It's easy to turn off if you don't want it.
- **Model and cost:** Haq uses Claude Opus 5.5 at medium effort. I'll report real cost per household after the first live run. You can switch models with `HAQ_MODEL`.
- **Python version:** neatlogs needs Python below 3.14, so I made a Python 3.12 environment in `.venv`.

.env is ready with both keys. Use Sonnet as the default model for the agent and evals to keep costs low. Test with one household first: a UP family where the mother is a widow and the father is a farmer with 2 acres. Then run the full evals and tell me the score. Confirm traces are showing in neatlogs.
